title: A Hidden Ocean Wave Is Raising the Sea on the West Coast
summary:
A giant wave you cannot see is raising sea levels on the West Coast of the United States. It is called a Kelvin wave. Scientists say more are coming.

A Kelvin wave is not a wave you could surf. It moves slowly under the ocean's surface and stretches for thousands of miles. Scientist Dillon Amaya called it "a planetary-scale wave."

These waves can form during El Niño years, when a big part of the Pacific Ocean gets much warmer than usual. The warm water travels east under the sea to South America. Then part of it moves north along the West Coast.

The wave does not cause floods by itself. But it makes floods more likely when big storms come. In early October, sea levels in parts of Southern California were about six to eight inches higher than normal. Then Tropical Storm Rachel flooded some neighborhoods.

The warmer water also brings surprises. A whale shark was spotted off San Diego. The next Kelvin wave may reach San Diego in late October or early November.
why_it_matters: Knowing when the sea will be higher helps families who live near the coast get ready for floods.
